readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Ark of the Witness
readings.subtitle: Betsal’ěl constructs the acacia wood and gold housing for the eternal covenant.
readings.text: [Exodus 37:1] And Betsal’ěl made <dn>את</dn> the ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, and a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high. [2] And he overlaid it with clean gold inside and outside, and made a moulding of gold all around it. [3] And he cast four rings of gold for it, for its four feet, two rings on its one side, and two rings on its other side. [4] And he made poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold. [5] And he put the poles into the rings at the sides of the ark, to lift <dn>את</dn> the ark.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Lid of Covering
readings.subtitle: The golden interface of restorative justice and the keruḇim of the divine presence are fashioned.
readings.text: [Exodus 37:6] And he made <dn>את</dn> a lid of atonement of clean gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide. [7] And he made <dn>את</dn> two keruḇim of beaten gold. He made them from the two ends of the lid of atonement, [8] one keruḇ at one end on this side, and the other keruḇ at the other end on that side. He made the keruḇim from the lid of atonement, from the two ends. [9] And the keruḇim spread out their wings above, and covered <dn>את</dn> the lid of atonement with their wings, with their faces toward each other, the faces of the keruḇim were turned toward the lid of atonement.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Table of Presence Bread
readings.subtitle: The pure gold table and utensils are prepared to bear the continuous provision.
readings.text: [Exodus 37:10] And he made <dn>את</dn> the table of acacia wood, two cubits long, and a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high. [11] And he overlaid it with clean gold, and made a moulding of gold all around it. [12] And he made a rim of a handbreadth all around it, and made a moulding of gold for the rim all around it. [13] And he cast four rings of gold for it, and put the rings on the four corners that were at its four legs. [14] The rings were next to the rim, as holders for the poles to lift <dn>את</dn> the table. [15] And he made <dn>את</dn> the poles of acacia wood to lift <dn>את</dn> the table, and overlaid them with gold. [16] And he made <dn>את</dn> the utensils which were on the table, its dishes, and its cups, and its bowls, and its jars for pouring, of clean gold.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Menorah of Unending Light
readings.subtitle: The geometric structure of the golden lampstand is beaten from a single talent.
readings.text: [Exodus 37:17] And he made <dn>את</dn> the lampstand of clean gold. He made the lampstand of beaten work, its base, and its shaft, its cups, its ornamental knobs, and its blossoms were from it. [18] And six branches came out of its sides: three branches of the lampstand out of one side, and three branches of the lampstand out of the other side. [19] There were three cups like almond flowers on one branch, with ornamental knob and blossom, and three cups like almond flowers on the other branch, a knob and a blossom – so for the six branches coming out of the lampstand. [20] And on the lampstand were four cups like almond flowers, its knobs and blossoms, [21] and a knob under the first two branches of the same, and a knob under the second two branches of the same, and a knob under the third two branches of the same, for the six branches coming out of it. [22] Their knobs and their branches were of it, all of it was one beaten work of clean gold. [23] And he made <dn>את</dn> its seven lamps, and <dn>את</dn> its snuffers, and <dn>את</dn> its trays, of clean gold. [24] He made <dn>את</dn> it of a talent of clean gold, and <dn>את</dn> all its utensils.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Altar of Ascending Incense
readings.subtitle: The square altar and the Qadosh anointing oil are compounded for exclusive service.
readings.text: [Exodus 37:25] And he made <dn>את</dn> the incense slaughter-place of acacia wood, a cubit long and a cubit wide, square, and two cubits high. Its horns were of it. [26] And he overlaid it with clean gold, its top and its sides all around, and its horns. And he made a moulding for it of gold all around it. [27] And he made two rings of gold for it under its moulding, at its two corners on both sides, as holders for the poles with which to lift it. [28] And he made <dn>את</dn> the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold. [29] And he made <dn>את</dn> the set-apart anointing oil and <dn>את</dn> the clean incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the perfumer.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Slaughter-Place of Ascending Offerings
readings.subtitle: The bronze interface for substitutionary atonement and restorative justice is built.
readings.text: [Exodus 38:1] And he made <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place of ascending offering of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide, square, and three cubits high. [2] And he made its horns on its four corners, the horns were of it. And he overlaid it with bronze. [3] And he made <dn>את</dn> all the utensils for the slaughter-place: <dn>את</dn> the pots, and <dn>את</dn> the shovels, and <dn>את</dn> the basins, and <dn>את</dn> the forks, and <dn>את</dn> the fire holders. He made all its utensils of bronze. [4] And he made a grating for the slaughter-place, a bronze network, under its rim, midway from the bottom. [5] And he cast four rings for the four corners of the bronze grating, as holders for the poles. [6] And he made <dn>את</dn> the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with bronze. [7] And he put <dn>את</dn> the poles into the rings on the sides of the slaughter-place, with which to lift <dn>את</dn> it. He made <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place hollow with boards.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Bronze Basin of Purification
readings.subtitle: The serving women surrender their bronze mirrors to craft the washing station for the priests.
readings.text: [Exodus 38:8] And he made <dn>את</dn> the basin of bronze and <dn>את</dn> its stand of bronze, from the bronze mirrors of the serving women who did service at the door of the Tent of Appointment.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Linen Perimeter
readings.subtitle: The fine woven linen sets the boundary of exclusivity for the Dwelling Place.
readings.text: [Exodus 38:9] And he made <dn>את</dn> the courtyard: for the south side the screens of the courtyard were of fine woven linen, one hundred cubits long, [10] their twenty columns and their twenty sockets, of bronze. The hooks of the columns and their bands were of silver. [11] And for the north side the screens were one hundred cubits long, their twenty columns and their twenty sockets, of bronze. The hooks of the columns and their bands were of silver. [12] And for the west side there were screens of fifty cubits, their ten columns and their ten sockets. The hooks of the columns and their bands were of silver. [13] And for the east side eastward, fifty cubits: [14] fifteen cubits of screens on the one side, with their three columns and their three sockets, [15] and fifteen cubits of screens the other side of the courtyard gate, on this side and that side, with their three columns and their three sockets. [16] All the screens of the courtyard all around were of fine woven linen. [17] And the sockets for the columns were of bronze, the hooks of the columns and their bands were of silver, and the overlay of their tops was of silver. And all the columns of the courtyard had bands of silver.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Gate of Access
readings.subtitle: The embroidered gate of blue, purple, and scarlet establishes the single entry point.
readings.text: [Exodus 38:18] And the covering for the gate of the courtyard was the work of an embroiderer, of blue and purple and scarlet material, and of fine woven linen, and twenty cubits long, and the height along its width was five cubits, corresponding to the screens of the courtyard. [19] And the columns were four, and their sockets of bronze four, their hooks were of silver, and the overlay of their tops and their bands was of silver. [20] And all <dn>את</dn> the pegs of the Dwelling Place, and of the courtyard all around, were of bronze.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Appointed Architects
readings.subtitle: Betsal’ěl and Oholiaḇ execute the exact geometric and physical specifications commanded by YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Exodus 38:21] These were the appointments of the Dwelling Place, the Dwelling Place of the Witness, which was appointed by the mouth of Mosheh, for the service of the Lěvites, by the hand of Ithamar, son of Aharon the priest. [22] And Betsal’ěl son of Uri, son of Ḥur, of the tribe of Yehuḏah, made <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh. [23] And with him: Oholiaḇ son of Aḥisamaḵ, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver and designer, an embroiderer in blue and purple and scarlet material, and in fine linen.

readings.section: The Architecture of the Dwelling Place
readings.title: The Economics of the Dwelling Place
readings.subtitle: A strict accounting of the gold, silver, and bronze contributed by the congregation.
readings.text: [Exodus 38:24] All the gold prepared for the work, in all the work of the set-apart place – and it was the gold of the wave offering – came to be twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty sheqels, according to the sheqel of the set-apart place. [25] And the silver from the ones counted of the congregation was one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five sheqels, according to the sheqel of the set-apart place: [26] a beqa, half a sheqel for a head, according to the sheqel of the set-apart place, for everyone passing over to those counted, from twenty years old and above, for six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty men. [27] And the hundred talents of silver were for casting <dn>את</dn> the sockets of the set-apart place and <dn>את</dn> the bases of the veil: one hundred sockets from the hundred talents, a talent for each socket. [28] And of the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five sheqels he made hooks for the columns, and overlaid <dn>את</dn> their tops, and made bands for them. [29] And the bronze of the wave offering was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred sheqels. [30] And with it he made <dn>את</dn> the sockets for the door of the Tent of Appointment, and <dn>את</dn> the bronze slaughter-place, and <dn>את</dn> the bronze grating for it, and <dn>את</dn> all the utensils for the slaughter-place, [31] and <dn>את</dn> the sockets for the courtyard all around, and <dn>את</dn> the bases for the courtyard gate, and <dn>את</dn> all the pegs for the Dwelling Place, and <dn>את</dn> all the pegs for the courtyard all around.

readings.title: The Weaving of Exclusivity
readings.subtitle: The blue, purple, and scarlet materials are woven to perfectly equip Aharon for his function.
readings.text: [Exodus 39:1] And of the blue and purple and scarlet material they made <dn>את</dn> woven garments, to do service in the set-apart place. And they made <dn>את</dn> the set-apart garments which were for Aharon, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh.

readings.title: The Shoulder Garment of Authority
readings.subtitle: The names of Yisra’ěl are permanently bound to the High Priest’s shoulders.
readings.text: [Exodus 39:2] And he made <dn>את</dn> the shoulder garment of gold, of blue and purple and scarlet material, and of fine woven linen. [3] And they beat out <dn>את</dn> sheets of gold and cut <dn>את</dn> it into threads, to work it in with the blue and purple and scarlet material, and the fine linen, the work of a skilled workman. [4] They made shoulder pieces for it to join it, it was joined at its two edges. [5] And the embroidered band of his shoulder garment that was on it was of the same work of gold, and blue and purple and scarlet material, and of fine woven linen, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh. [6] And they made <dn>את</dn> the shoham stones, set in plated work of gold, engraved as signets are engraved, according to the names of the sons of Yisra’ěl. [7] And he put them on the shoulders of the shoulder garment, stones of remembrance for the sons of Yisra’ěl, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh.

readings.title: The Breastplate of Righteous Judgment
readings.subtitle: The twelve tribes are geometrically ordered and set in four rows of precious stones.
readings.text: [Exodus 39:8] And he made <dn>את</dn> the breastplate, a work of a skilled workman, like the work of the shoulder garment, of gold, of blue and purple and scarlet material, and of fine woven linen. [9] It was square, they made the breastplate double, its length a span, its width a span, doubled. [10] And they filled it with four rows of stones: a row of ruby, a topaz, and an emerald was the first row; [11] and the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond; [12] and the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; [13] and the fourth row a beryl, a shoham, and a jasper – set in plated work of gold in their settings. [14] And the stones were according to the names of the sons of Yisra’ěl, twelve according to their names, engraved like a signet, each one with its own name according to the twelve tribes.

readings.title: Securing the Judgment
readings.subtitle: Golden chains and a blue cord permanently anchor the breastplate to the shoulder garment.
readings.text: [Exodus 39:15] And they made <dn>את</dn> braided chains of corded work for the breastplate at the ends, of clean gold. [16] And they made two settings of gold and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate. [17] And they put <dn>את</dn> the two cords of gold in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate. [18] And the two ends of the two cords they fastened in the two settings, and put them on the shoulder pieces of the shoulder garment in the front. [19] And they made two rings of gold and put them on the two ends of the breastplate, on the edge of it, which was on the inward side of the shoulder garment. [20] And they made two gold rings and put them on the two shoulder pieces, underneath the shoulder garment, on the front of it, close to its seam above the embroidered band of the shoulder garment. [21] And they bound <dn>את</dn> the breastplate by means of its rings to the rings of the shoulder garment with a blue cord, so that it would be above the embroidered band of the shoulder garment, and that the breastplate would not come loose from the shoulder garment, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh.

readings.title: The Blue Robe of Tsedek
readings.subtitle: The seamless blue robe is hemmed with pomegranates and golden bells to announce the High Priest's life.
readings.text: [Exodus 39:22] And he made <dn>את</dn> the robe of the shoulder garment of woven work, all of blue. [23] And the opening of the robe was in the middle, like the opening in a scaled armour, with a woven binding all around the opening, so that it would not tear. [24] And they made on the hem of the robe pomegranates of blue and purple and scarlet material, twined. [25] And they made <dn>את</dn> bells of clean gold, and put <dn>את</dn> the bells between the pomegranates on the hem of the robe all around between the pomegranates: [26] a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe, for the service, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh.

readings.title: The White Linen of Righteousness
readings.subtitle: The fine linen garments of service are prepared for Aharon and his sons.
readings.text: [Exodus 39:27] And they made <dn>את</dn> the long shirt of fine linen, the work of a weaver, for Aharon and his sons, [28] and <dn>את</dn> a turban of fine linen, and <dn>את</dn> the turban ornaments of fine linen, and <dn>את</dn> short trousers of fine woven linen, [29] and <dn>את</dn> a girdle of fine woven linen with blue and purple and scarlet material, the work of an embroiderer, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh.

readings.title: The Crown of Absolute Exclusivity
readings.subtitle: The golden plate officially declares Aharon as Qadosh to YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Exodus 39:30] And they made <dn>את</dn> the plate of the set-apart sign of dedication of clean gold, and wrote on it an inscription like the engraving of a signet: SET-APARTNESS TO <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [31] And they put on it a blue cord, to fasten it above on the turban, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh.
